question: Can a Muslim keep a dog to guard the home, or as an assistance dog for a special-needs child?
asked: A sister would like to get a dog to protect her house: she lives in a large house, somewhat isolated from other houses, and at times her husband travels for work, so she would feel safer having a dog on the property. Is this allowed? Another sister has a special-needs child, and the doctors have said a trained dog would help the child. What is the ruling on that?
answer:
So the answer is that we are all familiar that our Prophet ﷺ strongly discouraged owning a dog. It is strongly discouraged, and the hadith is in Bukhari and Muslim: our Prophet ﷺ said that whoever acquires a dog, or whoever owns a dog, that he doesn't need for his cultivation or for his sheep (basically shepherding, so the dog is protecting the sheep, or the dog is protecting the land or something), whoever acquires a dog not for those reasons, then every single day an amount of good deeds, the level or amount of a qirat, will be diminished. Some have said the qirat is like the mountain of Uhud; some have said smaller or larger. But basically, every single day a large amount of good deeds will be diminished from the good deeds that he is doing. So basically we are strongly discouraged, and this is the position of basically the vast majority.

Now, a lot of people... Remember, this is the rapid Q&A today, so I'm not going to go into a lot of detail. But a lot of people are confused: "Dogs are so cute, I want to have dogs," etc. Look, sometimes we do not understand the wisdom of a Shariah ruling, and sometimes we do. In this particular case, the most that can be said is that maybe it is because the saliva of the dog is considered najis.

By the way, it's only the saliva of the dog that is najis; this is the strongest position. As for the body of the dog, the hair of the dog, this is not najis. But the saliva of the dog: whatever the dog licks, you cannot pray on that or wear that. If the dog licks anything, you have to take that garment off and wash it, or wear another garment or whatever. And if the dog licks you, you have to wash yourself at that place before you pray, obviously. Otherwise, before that time, you don't have to immediately go and do that.

So the point being that some people say, "Why can't we have a dog?" And the response is: Allah knows best. Really, we do not have a specific reason. Maybe it's because of the najasah of the saliva; Allah knows best. Whatever the reason might be, the Qur'an has clearly allowed one category of dogs, and that is the dogs of hunting. It is explicit in Surah Al-Ma'idah: Allah 'azza wa jall says in the Qur'an that the dogs that you have trained to hunt, you may hunt with them, as long as you mention the name of Allah, and then you may eat from what they have caught for you.

So the Qur'an is explicit that hunting dogs are allowed. When you have hunting dogs, you will be around them, you will be training them, they will be jumping all over you, they will love you as dogs do, and the Qur'an allows this. So we have to be careful here about not going to extremes when it comes to the issue of dogs. Dogs by their nature are loyal and loving, and the fact that you're going to be training a hunting dog means it's more loyal to you than to anybody else. And this is explicitly allowed in the Qur'an. So a righteous man can have multiple dogs for hunting. It's not a matter of life and death; it's a matter of just pleasure hunting. You don't have to have a hunting dog.

So the Qur'an allows a dog for a reason, and the Sunnah allows it for other reasons: for example, agriculture, protecting the crops from any predators or animals that come and harm them; and also the shepherd dog, for a person who has a lot of sheep, so the dogs help in gathering the sheep and whatnot. And once again, these dogs will be like all the dogs that we know in our times: the loyalty of dogs, the love that the dogs have. They're going to be jumping up and down, they're going to be licking the master. This is the way that it goes; that's the way every single dog is. And the Shariah and the Sunnah allow for that to happen and consider it to be permissible.

Now, based on this, a number of 'ulama have said that this means any time there is, not even a hajah, but some benefit... Because see, again, a hunting dog is not a matter of life and death. I mean, if you really needed to, you would go shoot with a bow and arrow. You don't have to be starving to go and get a hunting dog. You can have a hunting dog for sport, you can have a hunting dog just as a passion, like you just want to. It's not something where you have to be dying or in a very dire situation. So if it is allowed for all of this, then many 'ulama, and this is the majority position, have allowed having dogs for any legitimate need.

The famous Shafi'i scholar al-Iraqi says in Tarh al-Tathrib, the famous commentary he has, that our Shafi'i scholars said it is allowed to acquire a dog for anybody who wishes to hunt, or anybody who wishes to guard vegetation, basically plantations and cultivation, or anybody who wishes to use it as a shepherd dog. So these three. Then he said: our madhhab has differed over any other reason, a fourth reason, for example to guard the house, or other types of purposes. Some scholars of our madhhab said it is not allowed, because these three are mentioned explicitly. However, the majority said, and this is the correct opinion, that you make analogy with these three, and any hajah, anything that is needed that a dog can help you with, you may acquire a dog for that.

And the Shafi'i scholar al-Khatib al-Shirbini as well says that it is allowed to acquire a dog for anybody who will use it to hunt, or anybody who will have any type of protection for cultivation or for animals. And it was then also allowed to train a puppy or a dog so that it can then be of benefit to the master, to the owner. So all of this is very clear.

And therefore, based on this, if you feel that a dog is going to be something that will give you... because again, the dog is in many ways far better than an alarm, because it has a sense when a human is coming and it's going to bark and scare the person, and it has other benefits as well. And therefore, if you feel that a dog is something that will help you, and definitely the other sister asked about a dog for a child with special needs: there is no question. A seeing dog for a person who cannot see, or a person who might have a type of issue, maybe ADHD or whatever, where having an animal will make that person calm, or whatever it might be: there is no question that this is more important than a hobby of hunting with a dog. **So there's no question that in such a circumstance, dogs would be allowed.**

And of course, a seeing dog, or a dog that is for a special-needs child, will be inside the house. And therefore all that should be done is that there should be one area of the house that is dedicated to the salah, and the dog should not be going over there. And before you pray, make sure that your clothes and your hands do not have any of the saliva. Other than that, you should really try your best not to have the protection dog inside the house. But in case you need to, and in case there is a hajah for this, make sure that there is an area that is definitely pure to pray in, and you would be allowed to have that.
